scope_basis: Guarantee backs the financial capacity behind a customs bond as well as its technology platform.
title: Afreximbank — BSMART Technology, EAC Customs Bond guarantee, 2026
description:
The announcing party's own sentences:

> Cairo, Egypt, 22 September 2026: African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) has issued a US$ 29 million guarantee to BSMART Technology Ltd to support the implementation and scaling of the EAC Customs Bond, the technology-enabled regional customs guarantee solution that facilitates the movement of goods across East African countries.

> Aimed at strengthening the financial capacity underpinning the EAC Customs Bond and supporting the transition to a more seamless digital and integrated customs environment, the facility will enable BSMART Technology Ltd to strengthen the implementation and market uptake of the EAC Customs Bond.
original_amount: US$29,000,000 — Afreximbank states the figure in dollars itself; no conversion written

scope_basis: Regional AI research and training network, AI strategy and digital skills.

Includes USD50,000 in prize funding for the AI4EAC Innovation Challenge's second edition (per the EAC's own 12 August 2026 release, raw/2026/2026-08-12-bmz-eac-ai4eac-innovation-challenge.md), which also names new partners Equity Group Holdings and the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) and introduces an Ebola Response Challenge track. scope_basis: Acquisition of a broadband and enterprise connectivity operator.
title: Axian Telecom (Yas) Acquisition of Wananchi Group — Zuku/Simbanet
description:
On 5–7 November 2025, Axian Telecom Fibre Ltd (trading as Yas) completed the acquisition of 99.63% of Wananchi Group Holdings Ltd for approximately USD 63 million (KES 9.6 billion). Wananchi Group operates Zuku (consumer broadband/IPTV, Kenya) and Simbanet (enterprise connectivity, Tanzania). The acquisition extends Axian's fixed broadband footprint into Kenya, Tanzania (integrated with existing Yas Tanzania) and Uganda. The deal was partly financed by the USD 600M 2025 bond (part of proceeds) and separately by an IFC loan of USD 25M plus USD 37.5M from partner lenders.

Recipient countries: KEN, UGA.
